title: Intricate alliterative and isosyllabic rules of the Welsh englyn
html_source:
The englyn is a Welsh/Cornish poem form as suggested in the text. There are many types of englynion, and several examples in Welsh are included in the link above. Here is an English-language englyn by novelist Robertson Davies.

The Old Journalist
He types his laboured column—weary drudge!
Senile, fudge and solemn;
Spare, editor, to condemn
These dry leaves of his autumn.

The repeating pattern of consonants (here, dg, mn) is known as a cynghanedd
